1.explanation: This reproduction shows that using String.replace(needle, replacementString) will interpret `$'` in the replacementString as a special token (the portion of the input string after the match). As a result, the placeholder and/or closing </script> get swallowed, the injection escapes the <script> block, and your page breaks. To fix, you must escape `$` sequences (e.g. replace every `$` with `$$`) or use a callback form of replace to inject raw text without interpreting special tokens.
1.bug_scenario: We have a simple HTML “template” with a placeholder comment inside a <script> tag, and we use JavaScript’s String.replace to inject the contents of another JS file into that placeholder. If the injected JS contains the sequence `$'`, replace will treat it as a special replacement pattern (meaning "insert everything after the match"), so your placeholder and the rest of the HTML get swallowed up or injected incorrectly. In the browser you’ll see that your injected code escapes the <script> block, the rest of the page breaks, and the devtools DOM shows a truncated or malformed script.
